projects.title: Smart Calculator
projects.tagline: A menu-driven calculator with history and error handling
projects.overview:
Build a command-line calculator that supports the four basic operations plus power and modulo.
It validates every input, refuses to divide by zero and keeps a history of all calculations —
exactly the kind of robust tool professionals write.

steps.title: Plan the operations
steps.text:
Store each operation in a dictionary that maps a symbol to a function. This avoids a long chain of `if/elif`
statements and makes adding new operations trivial.
steps.code:
operations = {
    "+": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "-": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "*": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "/": lambda a, b: a / b,
}
print(operations["*"](6, 7))

steps.title: Read numbers safely
steps.text: Users make typos. Wrap the conversion in `try/except` and keep asking until the input is valid.

steps.title: Calculate with protection
steps.text: Catch `ZeroDivisionError` so the program never crashes, and return a friendly message instead.

steps.title: Main loop and history
steps.text: Show a menu inside `while True`, store every result in a list and print the history when the user quits.

steps.title: Test it
steps.text: Run the full program in the terminal. Try invalid numbers, divide by zero, then quit with `q` to see your history.

projects.title: To-Do List Manager
projects.tagline: Add, complete, delete and save tasks to a file
projects.overview:
A productivity app every developer builds. Tasks are stored as dictionaries in a list, can be marked
as done or removed, and are saved to a JSON file so they survive between runs.

steps.title: Model a task
steps.text: Each task is a dictionary with a title, priority and done flag.
steps.code:
task = {"title": "Learn Python", "priority": "high", "done": False}
print(task["title"], "-", task["priority"])

steps.title: Load and save
steps.text: Use `json.dump` and `json.load` with a fallback when the file doesn't exist yet.

steps.title: Show the list
steps.text: Print each task with its number, a checkbox and priority.

steps.title: Handle commands
steps.text: Use `match` to react to add / done / delete / list / quit commands.

steps.title: Run and test
steps.text: Add a few tasks, complete one, delete one and quit. Run again — your tasks are still there!

projects.code:
import json

PATH = "tasks.json"


def load_tasks():
    try:
        with open(PATH) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []


def save_tasks(tasks):
    with open(PATH, "w") as f:
        json.dump(tasks, f, indent=2)


def show(tasks):
    if not tasks:
        print("  (no tasks yet)")
        return
    for i, t in enumerate(tasks, 1):
        mark = "✔" if t["done"] else " "
        print(f"  {i}. [{mark}] {t['title']}  ({t['priority']})")
    done = sum(t["done"] for t in tasks)
    print(f"  Progress: {done}/{len(tasks)} done")


def pick(tasks):
    try:
        n = int(input("  Task number: "))
        return tasks[n - 1] if 1 <= n <= len(tasks) else None
    except ValueError:
        return None


tasks = load_tasks()
print("=== To-Do Manager ===")
print("Commands: add, done, delete, list, quit")
while True:
    cmd = input("\n> ").strip().lower()
    match cmd:
        case "add":
            title = input("  Title: ").strip()
            priority = input("  Priority (low/medium/high): ").strip() or "medium"
            tasks.append({"title": title, "priority": priority, "done": False})
            print("  Added ✅")
        case "done":
            task = pick(tasks)
            if task:
                task["done"] = True
                print("  Completed:", task["title"])
            else:
                print("  Invalid number")
        case "delete":
            task = pick(tasks)
            if task:
                tasks.remove(task)
                print("  Deleted:", task["title"])
            else:
                print("  Invalid number")
        case "list":
            show(tasks)
        case "quit":
            save_tasks(tasks)
            print("Saved", len(tasks), "tasks. Bye!")
            break
        case _:
            print("  Unknown command")

projects.title: Python Quiz Game
projects.tagline: A scored multiple-choice quiz with shuffled questions
projects.overview:
Build an interactive quiz that shuffles its questions, checks answers, keeps score and finishes
with a grade. You'll practise data structures, randomness and clean output formatting.

    {"q": "Which keyword defines a function?",
     "options": ["func", "def", "lambda", "fn"], "answer": "b"},
]
print(len(questions), "question(s) ready")

steps.title: Shuffle
steps.text: Use `random.shuffle()` so every game is different.

steps.text: Print the options with letters a–d, read the answer and compare it with the correct letter.

steps.title: Grade the player
steps.text: Calculate the percentage and choose a grade with `if/elif`.

import random

questions = [
    {"q": "Which keyword defines a function?", "options": ["func", "def", "lambda", "fn"], "answer": "b"},
    {"q": "What does len('python') return?", "options": ["5", "6", "7", "Error"], "answer": "b"},
    {"q": "Which type is immutable?", "options": ["list", "dict", "tuple", "set"], "answer": "c"},
    {"q": "What is 2 ** 3?", "options": ["6", "8", "9", "5"], "answer": "b"},
    {"q": "Which method adds to a list?", "options": ["add()", "push()", "append()", "insert_end()"], "answer": "c"},
]

random.seed(42)
random.shuffle(questions)
score = 0
print("=== Python Quiz ===")
for number, item in enumerate(questions, 1):
    print(f"\nQ{number}. {item['q']}")
    for letter, option in zip("abcd", item["options"]):
        print(f"   {letter}) {option}")
    answer = input("Your answer: ").strip().lower()
    if answer == item["answer"]:
        score += 1
        print("   ✅ Correct!")
    else:
        correct = item["options"]["abcd".index(item["answer"])]
        print(f"   ❌ Wrong — the answer is {item['answer']}) {correct}")

percent = score / len(questions) * 100
if percent >= 80:
    grade = "Excellent 🏆"
elif percent >= 60:
    grade = "Good 👍"
else:
    grade = "Keep practising 💪"
print(f"\nScore: {score}/{len(questions)} ({percent:.0f}%) — {grade}")

projects.title: Password Generator
projects.tagline: Generate strong passwords and rate their strength
projects.overview:
Security matters. This tool generates cryptographically secure passwords with the `secrets` module,
lets the user choose which character sets to include, and rates password strength.

steps.title: Character pools
steps.text: The `string` module has ready-made pools of characters.
steps.code:
import string
print(string.ascii_lowercase)
print(string.digits)
print(string.punctuation)

steps.title: Secure random choice
steps.text: `secrets.choice` is safer than `random.choice` for passwords.
steps.code:
import secrets, string
print("".join(secrets.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(12)))

steps.title: Guarantee variety
steps.text: Pick at least one character from each selected pool, then fill and shuffle.

steps.title: Rate strength
steps.text: Score length and character variety to label the password Weak, Medium or Strong.

projects.code:
import secrets
import string


def generate(length=16, digits=True, symbols=True):
    pools = [string.ascii_lowercase, string.ascii_uppercase]
    if digits:
        pools.append(string.digits)
    if symbols:
        pools.append("!@#$%^&*?-_")
    chars = [secrets.choice(pool) for pool in pools]
    everything = "".join(pools)
    chars += [secrets.choice(everything) for _ in range(length - len(chars))]
    secrets.SystemRandom().shuffle(chars)
    return "".join(chars)


def strength(pw):
    score = 0
    score += len(pw) >= 8
    score += len(pw) >= 12
    score += any(c.islower() for c in pw)
    score += any(c.isupper() for c in pw)
    score += any(c.isdigit() for c in pw)
    score += any(not c.isalnum() for c in pw)
    return ["Very weak", "Very weak", "Weak", "Medium", "Good", "Strong", "Very strong"][score]


print("=== Password Generator ===")
length = int(input("Length (8-64): ") or 16)
length = max(8, min(64, length))
use_digits = input("Include digits? (y/n): ").lower() != "n"
use_symbols = input("Include symbols? (y/n): ").lower() != "n"
count = int(input("How many passwords? ") or 3)

for i in range(count):
    pw = generate(length, use_digits, use_symbols)
    print(f"{i + 1}. {'*' * 4}{pw[4:]}  →  {strength(pw)}  (length {len(pw)})")

print("\nCheck your own password:")
mine = input("Password: ")
print("Strength:", strength(mine))

import json

RAW = """{
  "city": "Dhaka",
  "country": "BD",
  "days": [
    {"day": "Mon", "min": 24, "max": 31, "condition": "sunny", "humidity": 62},
    {"day": "Tue", "min": 25, "max": 33, "condition": "cloudy", "humidity": 70},
    {"day": "Wed", "min": 23, "max": 29, "condition": "rain", "humidity": 88},
    {"day": "Thu", "min": 22, "max": 27, "condition": "storm", "humidity": 91},
    {"day": "Fri", "min": 24, "max": 32, "condition": "sunny", "humidity": 58}
  ]
}"""

ICONS = {"sunny": "☀️", "cloudy": "⛅", "rain": "🌧️", "storm": "⛈️"}


def c_to_f(c):
    return c * 9 / 5 + 32


data = json.loads(RAW)
unit = input("Units — C or F? ").strip().upper()
convert = c_to_f if unit == "F" else (lambda c: c)
symbol = "°F" if unit == "F" else "°C"

print(f"\n5-day forecast for {data['city']}, {data['country']}")
print(f"{'Day':<5}{'':<3}{'Min':>6}{'Max':>6}  {'Hum':>4}  Chart")
for d in data["days"]:
    lo, hi = convert(d["min"]), convert(d["max"])
    bar = "█" * int(d["max"] - 20)
    icon = ICONS.get(d["condition"], "❔")
    print(f"{d['day']:<5}{icon:<3}{lo:>6.0f}{hi:>6.0f}  {d['humidity']:>3}%  {bar}")

maxes = [d["max"] for d in data["days"]]
hottest = max(data["days"], key=lambda d: d["max"])
rainy = [d["day"] for d in data["days"] if d["condition"] in ("rain", "storm")]
print(f"\nAverage high: {convert(sum(maxes) / len(maxes)):.1f}{symbol}")
print(f"Hottest day: {hottest['day']} ({convert(hottest['max']):.0f}{symbol})")
print("Take an umbrella on:", ", ".join(rainy) if rainy else "no days")

projects.tagline: Track spending by category with reports and budgets
projects.overview:
Manage personal finances like a pro. Record expenses with categories, see totals per category,
compare against a budget and export everything to CSV for a spreadsheet.

steps.text: A list of dictionaries is perfect for tabular data.

expenses.append({"amount": 40, "category": "transport", "note": "fuel"})
print(sum(e["amount"] for e in expenses))

steps.title: Group by category
steps.text: Use a dictionary to accumulate totals per category.

steps.title: Draw a report
steps.text: Sort categories by amount and draw proportional bars.

steps.title: Export to CSV
steps.text: Use `csv.DictWriter` to save the expenses for Excel or Google Sheets.

projects.code:
import csv

BUDGET = 300.0
expenses = []

print("=== Expense Tracker ===")
print("Enter expenses as: amount category note   (blank line to finish)")
while True:
    line = input("> ").strip()
    if not line:
        break
    parts = line.split(maxsplit=2)
    try:
        amount = float(parts[0])
        category = parts[1].lower() if len(parts) > 1 else "other"
        note = parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else ""
    except ValueError:
        print("  Format: 12.50 food lunch")
        continue
    expenses.append({"amount": amount, "category": category, "note": note})

totals = {}
for e in expenses:
    totals[e["category"]] = totals.get(e["category"], 0) + e["amount"]
grand = sum(totals.values())

print("\n--- Spending by category ---")
for cat, amount in sorted(totals.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True):
    share = amount / grand if grand else 0
    print(f"{cat:<12}{amount:>8.2f}  {'■' * round(share * 20):<20} {share:.0%}")
print(f"{'TOTAL':<12}{grand:>8.2f}")

left = BUDGET - grand
if left < 0:
    print(f"⚠️  Over budget by {-left:.2f}!")
else:
    print(f"✅ {left:.2f} left of your {BUDGET:.0f} budget")

with open("expenses.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["amount", "category", "note"])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(expenses)
print(f"Exported {len(expenses)} expenses to expenses.csv")

projects.title: Smart File Organizer
projects.tagline: Automatically sort files into folders by type
projects.overview:
Automation is one of Python's superpowers. This script scans a messy folder and moves every file
into a sub-folder based on its extension (Images, Documents, Music…), then prints a report.
It works on a demo folder it creates itself, so it's safe to run.

steps.title: Explore a folder
steps.text: `Path.iterdir()` lists everything inside a folder.

steps.title: Map extensions
steps.text: A dictionary from category to extensions keeps rules readable.

steps.title: Move files
steps.text: `shutil.move()` moves a file. Create the destination with `mkdir(exist_ok=True)`.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Count how many files went into each folder and print a tidy summary.

projects.code:
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

CATEGORIES = {
    "Images": {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif", ".webp"},
    "Documents": {".pdf", ".docx", ".txt", ".md", ".xlsx"},
    "Music": {".mp3", ".wav", ".flac"},
    "Videos": {".mp4", ".mkv", ".mov"},
    "Code": {".py", ".kt", ".js", ".html", ".css"},
    "Archives": {".zip", ".rar", ".7z"},
}


def category_for(path):
    ext = path.suffix.lower()
    for name, extensions in CATEGORIES.items():
        if ext in extensions:
            return name
    return "Other"


def make_demo(folder):
    if folder.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(folder)
    folder.mkdir()
    names = ["holiday.jpg", "cv.pdf", "song.mp3", "app.py", "notes.txt", "clip.mp4",
             "logo.PNG", "backup.zip", "budget.xlsx", "random.xyz", "index.html", "photo.jpeg"]
    for name in names:
        (folder / name).write_text("demo")
    return len(names)


def organize(folder):
    report = {}
    for item in sorted(folder.iterdir()):
        if item.is_dir():
            continue
        category = category_for(item)
        target_dir = folder / category
        target_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        target = target_dir / item.name
        counter = 1
        while target.exists():
            target = target_dir / f"{item.stem}_{counter}{item.suffix}"
            counter += 1
        shutil.move(str(item), str(target))
        report.setdefault(category, []).append(item.name)
    return report


folder = Path("Downloads_demo")
count = make_demo(folder)
print(f"Created a messy folder with {count} files")
input("Press enter to organize it... ")
report = organize(folder)
print("\n=== Organized ===")
for category in sorted(report):
    files = report[category]
    print(f"📁 {category:<10} {len(files)} file(s): {', '.join(files)}")
print("\nFolders now:", ", ".join(sorted(p.name for p in folder.iterdir())))

USB-C Hub

$39.90View
""" class ProductParser(HTMLParser): def __init__(self): super().__init__() self.products = [] self.field = None def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs): attrs = dict(attrs) if tag == "div" and attrs.get("class") == "product": self.products.append({}) elif tag == "h2" and attrs.get("class") == "title": self.field = "title" elif tag == "span" and attrs.get("class") == "price": self.field = "price" elif tag == "a" and self.products: self.products[-1]["link"] = "https://shop.example.com" + attrs.get("href", "") def handle_data(self, data): if self.field and data.strip(): value = data.strip() if self.field == "price": value = float(value.replace("$", "")) self.products[-1][self.field] = value self.field = None parser = ProductParser() parser.feed(PAGE) products = parser.products print(f"Scraped {len(products)} products\n") limit = float(input("Show products under price: $") or 1000) cheap = sorted((p for p in products if p["price"] <= limit), key=lambda p: p["price"]) for p in cheap: print(f"{p['title']:<22}${p['price']:>8.2f} {p['link']}") with open("products.csv", "w", newline="") as f: writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["title", "price", "link"]) writer.writeheader() writer.writerows(products) print("\nSaved all products to products.csv") print(f"Average price: ${sum(p['price'] for p in products) / len(products):.2f}")

projects.title: Student Grade Analyzer
projects.tagline: Statistics, rankings and report cards from class data
projects.overview:
Teachers and schools love automation. Load a class's marks from CSV text, compute averages, letter grades,
rankings and subject statistics, find top performers and print beautiful report cards.
features: Average and letter grade per student

steps.title: Read the data
steps.text: `csv.DictReader` turns each row into a dictionary keyed by the header.
steps.code:
import csv, io
data = "name,math\nAli,90\nSara,75\n"
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(data)):
    print(row["name"], int(row["math"]))

steps.title: Grade function
steps.text: Convert an average into A–F using `if/elif`.

steps.title: Statistics
steps.text: `statistics.mean`, `median` and `stdev` describe each subject.

steps.title: Ranking
steps.text: Sort students by average with `sorted(..., key=..., reverse=True)`.

steps.title: Report card
steps.text: Look up a student by name and print every subject with a bar.

projects.code:
import csv
import io
import statistics

DATA = """name,math,physics,english,programming
Ali,88,79,92,95
Sara,95,91,85,98
John,72,65,80,70
Mia,60,58,75,66
Omar,91,87,70,89
Lina,45,52,61,58
"""

SUBJECTS = ["math", "physics", "english", "programming"]


def letter(avg):
    for limit, grade in [(90, "A"), (80, "B"), (70, "C"), (60, "D")]:
        if avg >= limit:
            return grade
    return "F"


students = []
for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(DATA)):
    marks = {s: int(row[s]) for s in SUBJECTS}
    avg = statistics.mean(marks.values())
    students.append({"name": row["name"], "marks": marks, "avg": avg, "grade": letter(avg)})

ranking = sorted(students, key=lambda s: s["avg"], reverse=True)
print("🏆 Class ranking")
for pos, s in enumerate(ranking, 1):
    medal = {1: "🥇", 2: "🥈", 3: "🥉"}.get(pos, "  ")
    print(f"{medal} {pos}. {s['name']:<6} {s['avg']:6.2f}  {s['grade']}")

print("\n📊 Subject statistics")
print(f"{'Subject':<13}{'Mean':>7}{'Median':>8}{'StDev':>7}{'Top':>6}")
for subject in SUBJECTS:
    scores = [s["marks"][subject] for s in students]
    print(f"{subject:<13}{statistics.mean(scores):>7.1f}{statistics.median(scores):>8.1f}"
          f"{statistics.stdev(scores):>7.1f}{max(scores):>6}")

print("\n📈 Grade distribution")
for g in "ABCDF":
    count = sum(s["grade"] == g for s in students)
    print(f"  {g}: {'█' * count} {count}")

name = input("\nReport card for: ").strip().title()
student = next((s for s in students if s["name"] == name), None)
if student:
    print(f"\n— Report card: {student['name']} —")
    for subject, mark in student["marks"].items():
        print(f"  {subject:<12}{mark:>4}  {'▇' * (mark // 10)}")
    print(f"  Average {student['avg']:.1f}  →  Grade {student['grade']}")
else:
    print("Student not found")

projects.title: Terminal Snake Game
projects.tagline: The classic Snake game on a text grid, controlled with W A S D
projects.overview:
The grand finale! Build the classic Snake game on a text grid. The snake moves with W/A/S/D commands,
eats food to grow, and the game ends when it hits a wall or itself. You'll combine data structures
(deque), coordinates, game state, randomness and rendering — everything you've learned.
features: Snake stored as a deque of coordinates

steps.title: Represent the snake
steps.text: A `deque` of `(row, col)` tuples — add a new head at the front, remove the tail at the back.
steps.code:
from collections import deque
snake = deque([(2, 2), (2, 1), (2, 0)])
snake.appendleft((2, 3))
snake.pop()
print(list(snake))

steps.title: Draw the board
steps.text: Loop over rows and columns and choose a character for each cell.

steps.title: Move
steps.text: Map W/A/S/D to direction vectors and compute the next head position.

steps.title: Collisions & food
steps.text: End the game on walls or self-collision. Grow when the head reaches the food.

steps.title: Game loop
steps.text: Read a string like `ddds` each turn so you can make several moves at once, and type `q` to quit.
